content.text: Live client metadata confirms the important detail: Codex publishes two portless loopback callbacks, while the runtime request uses `127.0.0.1:49188`. The error is being raised even earlier than the consent screen—while Skillplane/McpFn normalizes that fetched metadata—so I’m checking whether the deployed validator is rejecting the portless loopback document itself or the later port substitution.

This happens because Skillplane rejects one entry in Codex’s client metadata before it even compares the requested callback.

Codex currently publishes:

- `http://127.0.0.1/callback/zrStvbHj9pRN`
- `http://localhost/callback/zrStvbHj9pRN`

Your runtime callback is:

- `http://127.0.0.1:49188/callback/zrStvbHj9pRN`

McpFn already supports that dynamic port correctly. However, its default policy treats `localhost` redirects as opt-in. Skillplane does not provide `redirectPolicy.allowLocalhostLoopback`, so the second metadata entry causes the entire `redirect_uris` array to fail with the generic `unsafe or malformed URI` message.

I reproduced the exact behavior:

- Default policy: `invalid_client_metadata`
- With `allowLocalhostLoopback: true`: metadata validates
- The port-bearing callback then matches as `loopback-dynamic-port`

The missing policy is in [plugin.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/plugin.ts:135). Existing coverage only tests a numeric, already-port-bearing loopback callback and therefore misses Codex’s real two-entry metadata document: [oauth.test.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/oauth.test.ts:183).

This remains broken on the latest `origin/main` (`3654545`), even after the McpFn upgrade to `@mcpfn/auth@0.0.3`.

The narrow fix is to pass:

```ts
redirectPolicy: {
  allowLocalhostLoopback: true,
  allowDynamicLoopbackPort: true,
}
```

and add a regression test using Codex’s exact metadata shape. Non-loopback redirect matching can remain strict. Dynamic loopback ports are expected for native applications under [RFC 8252 §7.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8252.html#section-7.3).
